Knew I wanted to work with computers when I was 7 years old. Was the guy who made the dating app for my high school, local computer stores ran my code, taught computer lab stuff at university, worked for top orgs in my 30 years old career and seen / experienced quite a lot. So why are things different now? It is because AI is not a calculator that augments you. I will use my Cybertruck as an example. Either I am driving or my truck it is driving. We are not both driving at the same time to accomplish the goal of getting somewhere. A couple years ago it would get you killed if you were not paying attention. Today I have been saved a few times because the truck was driving rather than me. The technology developed today is the worst it is ever going to be and it is really really good already. Not the stuff you might have played with but the stuff you don’t have access to. Stop thinking of AI like it is in its final form. Its final form is a brain better than all brains collectively on earth. It is common for knowledge workers to think they will always be relevant in their field. Something is going to be completed soon that is more knowledgeable in all things than everyone combined. It will be a double bad because the relevance of knowledge workers is gone (manual. —> robots next) and you will probably not have access to this “something”. Everyone can’t have the equivalent of a nuclear bomb. On a positive note there is still some time to enjoy coffee and hang with people who have not realized.
